recipe.positive: Visual style (follow exactly): blue-and-white porcelain underglaze decoration technique applied to the entire scene: cobalt-blue only on a white porcelain ground, fine contour lines filled with graded 'fen-shui' wash (dark to light), pooled darker blue dots where brush pauses, repeating ceramic border motifs (wave, ruyi cloud, lotus scroll) used as frames and pattern fills, faint glaze sheen and tiny crackle. The scene itself fills the whole requested image frame as painted decoration; do not place the entire artwork on a photographed or isolated vase or plate; vessels explicitly requested by the brief remain valid depicted props. Draw with fine Chinese-brush contour lines in deep cobalt, using graded fen-shui wash to model forms in several tonal depths from dark to light. Place small pooled dark cobalt dots visibly at brush pauses, line ends, petal bases, fold corners and leaf tips. Use repeating ceramic border motifs (wave, ruyi cloud, lotus scroll) as frames and pattern fills, subordinate to the main subject. Keep the palette strictly cobalt blue and porcelain white with a faint glaze sheen and tiny crackle. Principal subjects, identities, actions and relationships follow the current brief, not the reference board. Do not add extra people, deities, animals or a new narrative theme. Ordinary supporting scene details and the source-style ornamental motifs may support the requested scene; when the brief sets an exact count or says only, preserve that restricted inventory. Borrow technique, never the reference scene, props, composition or lettering. Do not use hatching, cross-hatching, engraving, pen-and-ink, pencil or etching strokes, stippled shading, or photographic volume modelling.
hard_constraints: Every colour is a cobalt tone or porcelain white, so the entire scene is rendered in blue tonal depths on white.
Fine contour lines are filled with graded fen-shui wash from dark to light.
Small pooled dark cobalt dots are clearly visible at brush pauses, line ends and petal or fold bases.
Repeating ceramic border motifs (wave, ruyi cloud, lotus scroll) are used as frames and pattern fills and stay subordinate to the main subject.

The requested scene fills the entire image frame as painted decoration. Do not present the entire artwork on a photographed or isolated ceramic object; explicitly requested vessels remain valid props within the scene.
The palette is strictly cobalt blue and porcelain white with faint glaze sheen and tiny crackle.
Do not use hatching, cross-hatching, engraving, pen-and-ink, pencil or etching strokes, stippled shading, or photographic volume modelling.

整幅是青花绘饰，场景铺满画幅

translation_rules.people: 人物的脸、发型和衣着只来自内容 brief，现代衣着照画；肤色与衣色都以蓝色深浅表达，不古装化。
translation_rules.animals: Render the requested animal as painted blue-and-white underglaze decoration. Use fine cobalt Chinese-brush contour lines and graded fen-shui dark-to-light wash to describe its species, coat shapes, anatomy, pose and expression. Contours may be lifted and re-started where needed; neither a single uninterrupted contour nor hard stepped flat wash blocks is required. Preserve the species and relationships specified by the brief. Use small pooled deep cobalt dots where the brush pauses, faint glaze sheen and tiny crackle; no photographic volume, hatching or cross-hatching. Any wave, ruyi or lotus ornament decorates an existing surface requested by the brief, never an added flower plant or other scene object.

anchor.isolation: Transfer only the cobalt brush contours, the graded fen-shui wash tones (soft wet transitions between cobalt depths, dark at edge reading through mid cobalt into pale blue or bare porcelain white), the pooled dark dots and the faint crackled glaze technique from this reference board. Do not reproduce its title, labels, swatches, panel grid, border bands, landscape strip, sample figures, flowers as layout or composition. Do not copy any content of the reference board: its people, animals (such as its sleeping cat), cups and vessels, books, window, reading room, furniture, decorative layout, poses or arrangement. Draw people, animals, cups, books, windows, rooms or furniture only when the current brief itself asks for them, and then compose them fresh from the brief's own wording, never from the board's scene. When the brief gives no setting, use the crackled porcelain-glaze ground of the technique instead of adding a room or scenery from the board. Principal subjects, identities, actions and relationships follow the current brief, not the reference board. Do not add extra people, deities, animals or a new narrative theme. Ordinary supporting scene details and the source-style ornamental motifs may support the requested scene; when the brief sets an exact count or says only, preserve that restricted inventory. Borrow technique, never the reference scene, props, composition or lettering.; reproduce no writing from the board, and add text only where the brief explicitly requests it, spelled exactly as given.
